nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with a finite set of states $Q$, and suppose the syntactic monoid of the language accepted by $M$ is finite. Then that syntactic monoid has at most $|Q|^{|Q|}$ elements.
nodes.title: Endofunction bound for the syntactic monoid

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA accepting the language $L$, and suppose that the transition monoid of $M$ and the syntactic monoid of $L$ are both finite. Then the syntactic monoid of $L$ has at most as many elements as the transition monoid of $M$.
nodes.title: The syntactic monoid is no larger than the transition monoid

nodes.summary: If $Q$ is a finite set, then the monoid of state transformations of $Q$, consisting of all functions $Q \to Q$ multiplied in diagrammatic order, is finite.
nodes.title: Finitely many state transformations

nodes.summary: If $L$ is a regular language, then the syntactic monoid of $L$ is finite.
nodes.title: Regular languages have finite syntactic monoids

nodes.summary: For every DFA $M$ with a finite set of states, the transition monoid of $M$ is finite.
nodes.title: Transition monoids of finite automata are finite

nodes.summary: A language $L$ is regular if and only if the syntactic monoid of $L$ is finite.
nodes.title: Regular languages are those with finite syntactic monoid

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with start state $q_0$ and accepting states $F$. The map sending each word to the element of the transition monoid of $M$ that it induces recognizes the language accepted by $M$, with accepting set the elements $f$ of the transition monoid such that $f(q_0) \in F$: a word is accepted by $M$ exactly when the transformation it induces sends $q_0$ into $F$.
nodes.title: The transition monoid recognizes the accepted language

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA with start state $q_0$ and accepting states $F$. The transition morphism of $M$, from words to state transformations, recognizes the language accepted by $M$ through the accepting transformations of $M$: a word is accepted by $M$ exactly when the transformation it induces sends $q_0$ into $F$.
nodes.title: The transition morphism recognizes through accepting transformations

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ with set of states $Q$, start state $q_0$ and accepting states $F$, the accepting transformations of $M$ are the state transformations $f$ of $Q$ with $f(q_0) \in F$.
nodes.title: Accepting transformations of a DFA

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ accepting the language $L$, this is the monoid homomorphism from the transition monoid of $M$ to the syntactic monoid of $L$ that sends the transformation induced by each word $w$ to the syntactic class of $w$.
nodes.title: The transition monoid maps to the syntactic monoid

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
